description: Merging stack images is NOT Renovate's job any more: .github/workflows/renovate-pr-review.yml reviews every stack PR (image delta + Claude risk verdict), publishes the verdict as the `renovate-review` commit status - a required check on main - and merges only the green ones (no-op or RISK: LOW) in the 05:00-06:00 window. Renovate still automerges github-actions bumps itself - they touch no stack and redeploy nothing, and they get a green renovate-review so the required check never deadlocks them.

No release-age soak: open a PR for the newest release as soon as it appears. Dropped minimumReleaseAge because fast-releasing images kept resetting the soak clock and stranded PRs needing hand-merges.

ignorePrAuthor: match Renovate's own PRs by branch name, not by PR author. It is NOT set here - it is a global-only option, and Renovate answers `ignorePrAuthor` in renovate.json with a config warning ("cannot be configured within a repository's config file") and then ignores it. It lives as RENOVATE_IGNORE_PR_AUTHOR in .github/workflows/renovate.yml instead. Renovate authenticates with a GitHub App installation token, so its PRs are authored by the App's bot user - and were authored by the classic PAT's owner before that. Without it, changing the bot identity makes every already-open PR invisible to Renovate and it opens a duplicate for each one: it sat unset (as repo config) from 2026-08-22 to 2026-09-08, and PR #129 (portainer v2.44.0, opened under the PAT owner) went unseen for 40 days until it was hand-merged. Nothing but Renovate opens renovate/* branches in this repo.

rebaseWhen=conflicted: do NOT rebase branches merely because they are behind main. With automerge on, Renovate's default (auto) rebases every open branch as soon as main moves - and Renovate merges at most one PR per run, so each morning's single merge pushed a new commit onto all remaining branches, reset their check-runs to pending, and left them unmergeable until the next run. Result: exactly one merge per day (always the daily github-runner digest PR) while everything else piled up. Branch protection on main has strict=false, so a behind-base branch merges fine; the rebase bought nothing. Stacks live in separate folders, so real conflicts are rare - and those still rebase.

customManagers.description: The WebTunnel server version stacks/a1-vps-webtunnel/Dockerfile builds. Go datasource, i.e. proxy.golang.org: gitlab.torproject.org bot-walls automated clients.

The lyrebird (obfs4 transport) version stacks/a1-vps-tor-bridge/Dockerfile builds. Its tags are lyrebird-X.Y.Z, not vX.Y.Z, so proxy.golang.org lists no versions and the go datasource sees nothing: read the tags over git instead. The build itself still fetches the source through the Go module proxy.

Go modules stacks/caddy/Dockerfile compiles into the edge binary: the xcaddy --with plugins, and the --replace overrides that force patched versions of dependencies Caddy and the plugins still pin to vulnerable ones. A --with depName is the module root (host/owner/repo), so the crowdsec-bouncer http and appsec packages are one dependency and move together.

packageRules.description: Keep every stack image pinned by digest; Renovate refreshes the digest too.
Bundle minor+patch+digest per stack folder into one PR. One merge = one stack redeploy (deploy-stacks fires a webhook per changed stacks/<name>/).

Renovate does NOT merge stack images — .github/workflows/renovate-pr-review.yml does. Every stack PR, whatever the update type, gets the two-layer review (registry-API image delta + a Claude risk verdict) and is merged only if it comes back a no-op for our arch or RISK: LOW; that workflow's window-merge job does the merging, inside the same 05:00-06:00 redeploy window Renovate used to merge in. Why this rule stopped saying automerge: a minor bump is not evidence of a small change — mealie v3.20.1 -> v3.22.0 (PR #92) carried v3.21.0's new OIDC email_verified requirement, which would have auto-merged at 05:00 and locked every account out of a stack with no password login. Renovate keeps OPENING the PRs; deciding is the workflow's job.

Minor bumps: label for visibility. CalVer images (authentik = 2026.M.P, etc.) report a month bump as 'minor' but ship DB migrations / breaking config — and even plain semver minors do (see the mealie note above), which is why nothing merges without the review workflow clearing it.
Major bumps get their own PR (not bundled with the grouped minor+patch+digest) + label for visibility.

Stateful / blast-radius-critical images (databases, cache, SSO, and the edge's own Caddy build): a bad bump means data loss, full auth lockout (authentik fronts the proxied services), or every site down (ghcr.io/drizzelat/nas-caddy is built from this repo, so its digest PR shows a new digest but not which branch built it). Since the review workflow now gates every stack PR, this rule no longer changes what merges — it keeps the needs-manual-review label so these PRs are obvious in the list and in the GitHub email, and it keeps automerge pinned false in case the docker-compose rule above is ever relaxed. immich-app/postgres is here too (its major/minor/patch are disabled below, so only digests move). Keep this list in sync with MERGE_SKIP_IMAGES in renovate-pr-review.yml, which is what actually holds these PRs back from the sweep.

Komodo is the CONTROL PLANE (docs/runbooks/setup-operations/komodo-migration.md F2): Core and all three peripheries must move together, a v2 minor can break the Core-periphery transport, and the peripheries are hand-applied, so a merged bump deploys nothing on its own and leaves every host drifting until someone applies it. Grouped so Core and Periphery arrive in one PR. Never swept up: both images are on MERGE_SKIP_IMAGES in renovate-pr-review.yml, and mongo sits in the stateful rule above.

FileBrowser Quantum ships two tag lines from one repo: `<x.y.z>-stable` and `<x.y.z>-beta` (the 2.x rewrite). BOTH are semver prereleases, so a `-stable` pin is itself unstable and Renovate will happily offer `2.0.5-beta` as the next major. Constrain it to the stable line; moving to 2.x is a hand-edit once it ships stable. Same class of trap as the portainer-ee tag lines above.

MariaDB stays on the 12.3 LTS line. Everything after it (12.4+, 13.x) is a rolling release that stops getting patches as soon as the next one ships, and a major is a one-way datadir upgrade (docs/services/romm.md). Moving to the next LTS is a hand-edit. PR #407 (13.0) was closed for this.

komodo-mongo stays on MongoDB 8.0, a major release with a five-year lifecycle. Minor lines (8.2, 8.3) lose patches when the next one ships and cannot be skipped: each hop is a binary upgrade plus an FCV bump on a standalone datadir. PR #377 (8.0.30 -> 8.3.11) was closed for this.

App images that run irreversible DB schema migrations on first boot: gate MAJOR only to manual review. The deploy auto-rollback reverts the compose pin but NOT a migrated database, so a bad major = old image can't read the new schema = restore-from-dump. patch/minor/digest go through the review sweep like any other stack PR. Both immich images are listed so server + machine-learning never diverge across a major.
immich's custom Postgres uses a bespoke vendor tag (18-vectorchordX.Y.Z); only follow it by digest. Bump the tag manually per immich release notes.

GitHub Actions updates (actions/checkout etc.): auto-merge EVERY update type, including major. NO automergeSchedule — action bumps don't redeploy stacks, so the 05:00-06:00 redeploy window doesn't apply; merge as soon as checks pass. Digests stay pinned via helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests. Low blast radius: a bad action bump breaks CI (caught immediately, revert the pin), never a running service.

Inputs of the self-built Tor bridge images (stacks/a1-vps-webtunnel/Dockerfile and stacks/a1-vps-tor-bridge/Dockerfile: the WebTunnel server and lyrebird versions, the golang builder tag, and the thetorproject/obfs4-bridge image the start scripts are copied from): automerge, like github-actions. Merging one only rebuilds the image - build-webtunnel-image.yml or build-obfs4-image.yml pushes a new digest or tag, and that reaches the A1 as an ordinary docker-compose PR, which renovate-pr-review.yml still gates. Hand-merging these would stall exactly the security fixes a self-built image has to keep taking. They get a green renovate-review (no stack image moved), so the required check never blocks them.

Everything stacks/caddy/Dockerfile builds from - both caddy base images and the Go modules of the customManager above - in one PR. Merging it only rebuilds ghcr.io/drizzelat/nas-caddy on main (build-caddy-image.yml); the edge moves when the digest PR that follows is merged by hand (MERGE_SKIP_IMAGES). One PR per batch = one build and one digest PR, not one of each per module.
